questions.question:
**In the following question, some part of the sentence may have errors. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select 'No error'.**

Hardly had I reached the (1)/ exhibition where I learnt (2)/ about the major robbery. (3)/ No Error (4)
questions.solution:
The error lies in the part 2, in which ‘where’ has been incorrectly used. The correct word to be used here is ‘when’. The first part of the sentence mentions of the time or time-frame when the narrator had just reached, therefore, the use of ‘when’ must follow.

The correct sentence is – **Hardly had I reached the exhibition when I learnt about the major robbery.**

questions.question:
**In the following question, some part of the sentence may have errors. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select 'No error'.**

No sooner (1) had I walked in through the (2) door than the phone rang. (3)
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option 4**.

**'No sooner**' in a sentence is followed by the** past participle **form of a **verb**, accompanied by** 'than'** followed by the another verb in the **simple past** form.

questions.question:
**In the following question, the sentence given with blank to be filled in with an appropriate word. Select the correct alternative out of the four and indicate it by selecting the appropriate option.**

He _____ to the problem of air pollution in his speech.
questions.solution:
The word ‘adverted’ means ‘taking reference of something while speaking or mentioning of something’. In the given blank, the speaker is ‘adverting’ of the problem of air pollution in his speech.

‘Averted’ means turning something away. ‘Exclaimed’ means a sudden cry or outburst of emotion, and ‘mentioned’ means giving reference. Out of all the given words, ‘adverted’ is the most appropriate.

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the word opposite in meaning to the word given.**

Evanescent
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Enticing**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"Evanescent"** means something that is quickly fading or disappearing; it is often used to describe something transient or fleeting. (क्षणिक)

 
 
• **Example: **The beauty of a sunset is evanescent, lasting only for a few moments.
 
 
 
• **"Enticing"** refers to something that attracts or tempts someone; it is appealing or alluring. (आकर्षक)
 
 
• **Example: **The aroma of freshly baked bread was enticing to everyone in the room.
 
 
 
• Hence, we can infer that the opposite of **'Evanescent' **is **'Enticing'**.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Enticing**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Fleeting** (क्षणिक): Lasting for a very short time.

 
 
• **Example:** The happiness from winning the lottery was fleeting.
 
 
 
• **Erratic** (अनियमित): Not even or regular in pattern or movement; unpredictable.
 
 
• **Example: **His erratic behavior made it difficult to predict what he would do next.
 
 
 
• **Elusive** (पकड़ में न आने वाला): Difficult to find, catch, or achieve.
 
 
• **Example:** The elusive thief was finally caught by the police.

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the word opposite in meaning to the word given.**

Panegyric
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 2** i.e. Criticism.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"Panegyric"** means a public speech or published text in praise of someone or something. (प्रशंसा)

 
 
• **Example:** The author wrote a panegyric on the life and achievements of the Nobel laureate.
 
 
 
• **"Criticism"** refers to the expression of disapproval of someone or something based on perceived faults or mistakes. (आलोचना)
 
 
• **Example:** The movie received a lot of criticism for its weak plot and poor character development.
 
 
 
• Hence, we can infer that the opposite of **'Panegyric'** is **'Criticism'**.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 2** i.e. Criticism.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Noxious** (हानिकारक): Harmful, poisonous, or very unpleasant.

 
 
• **Example:** The factory was fined for releasing noxious chemicals into the river.
 
 
 
• **Fantasy** (काल्पनिक): The faculty or activity of imagining things, especially things that are impossible or improbable.
 
 
• **Example:** The book is a perfect blend of reality and fantasy.
 
 
 
• **Grandeur** (वैभव): Splendor and impressiveness, especially of appearance or style.
 
 
• **Example:** The grandeur of the palace left the visitors in awe.

questions.question:
**The question below consists of a set of labelled sentences. Out of the four options given, select the most logical order of the sentences to form a coherent paragraph.**

P: He raised his voice against idol-worship.

Q: People are generally very open and accept social changes with a positive attitude.

R: Swami Dayanand Saraswati is remembered with reverence and affection among the social reformers of the nineteenth century.

S: India is a country which respects spiritualism much more than materialism.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__SQRP__**

**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is an example of a Sentence Jumble. 
 
• The first statement of a sentence jumbled question is usually an independent general statement, a noun, a universal fact, the starting of an incident.
 
• Part S will be the first sentence because the sentence is an independent statement and introduces the subject 'spiritualism'.
 
• Part Q will be the next sentence because it supports the statement S by stating how 'spiritualism' is respected in India.
 
• Part R will be the next sentence because it tells us **about Swami Dayanand Saraswati **being one of the social reformers.
 
• Lastly, Part P will be used because it tells us more about Swami Dayanand Saraswati.

Correct Answer:__ *India is a country which respects spiritualism much more than materialism. People are generally very open and accept social changes with a positive attitude. Swami Dayanand Saraswati is remembered with reverence and affection among the social reformers of the nineteenth century. He raised his voice against idol-worship.*

questions.question:
**In the following question, a sentence has been given in Active/Passive voice. Out of four alternatives suggested, select the one which best expresses the same sentence in Passive/Active voice.**

Please guide me.

options.text: You are requested to guide me.
You have been requested to guide me.
You were requested to guide me.
You are being requested to guide me.

questions.solution: The sentence ‘please guide me’ does not showcase the presence of any present, past or future, ‘you have been’ and ‘you were’ are ruled out. The sentence ‘you are requested to guide me’ is the most correct passive form of the given question.

questions.question:
**In the following question, a sentence has been given in Direct/Indirect speech. Out of the four alternatives suggested, select the one which best expresses the same sentence in Indirect/Direct speech.**

The teacher said, "The Earth revolves around the sun."

options.text: The teacher said that the Earth is being revolving around the sun.
The teacher said that the Earth revolves around the sun.
The teacher said that the Earth revolved around the sun.
The teacher said that the Earth had been revolving around the sun.

questions.solution: In general rules of direct to indirect conversion, the word ‘revolves’ could have been converted to ‘revolved’, however, as the revolution of Earth around the Sun is a universal truth, the word ‘revolves’ would remain unchanged.

questions.question: The _____ of energy in India are met from both commercial
questions.solution: With the word ‘met’ some need or requirement needs to be fulfilled, therefore, the correct word for the blank is ‘requirements’.

questions.question: and non commercial sources. The most _____ sources of energy today are coal and natural gas
questions.solution: Out of the given words, the most meaningful words to fill with ‘sources of energy’ would be ‘vital’ and ‘important’. ‘Important’ makes a better fit as we can hardly have any vital sources of energy.

questions.question: On the other hand, firewood, cow-dung cakes and vegetable waste etc. _____ non commercial forms of energy.
questions.solution: Constitutes means making or forming, which makes the sentence apt. On the other hand, the mentioned sources of energy cannot combine, mix or collaborate to form non-commercial forms of energy because ‘combine’ and mix’ would mean absolute merging, which is impossible, while ‘collaborates’ is only used for the living forms.

questions.question: While non commercial forms of energy _____ demand,
questions.solution: ‘Need the demand’, ‘shed the demand’ and ‘rests the demand’ make no meaning with reference to the given sentence. The appropriate word here is ‘meet’ as the demand is ‘met’.

questions.question: coal is the _____ source of commercial energy in India.
questions.solution: In India, coal is the widest used source of energy, therefore, from the given words in the options, ‘smallest’, ‘heaviest’ and hardest’ get ruled out. The appropriate fit is ‘largest’.
